pricing.description: cost model: illustrative teaching defaults, or cited AWS us-east-1 / Google Cloud us-central1 / Azure East US on-demand prices

commitment.description: with a real pricing profile: a 1- or 3-year commitment (savings plan, reserved instances, committed use) at published rates, no upfront; usage prices are not discounted

id.description: Unique id, also used as the display name unless `name` is set

kind.description: Component type — see list_components for capacities, latency and price

tier.description: Vertical size: S ×1, M ×2, L ×4 capacity

instances.description: server/worker/llm: horizontal instances (reachable only behind lb/gateway/queue)

limit.description: gateway/llmapi/external/kv rate limit or function max concurrency, req/s

timeoutMs.description: client deadline; slower responses count as failures

fallback.description: serve a degraded response while the breaker is open

routing.description: split evenly (default), call all children in parallel, or fail over in order

stallRate.description: share of requests that hit a rare stall (GC pause, compaction, noisy neighbour)

fanout.description: each call goes to N partitions of the callee in parallel; the caller waits for the slowest (scatter-gather)

queueS.description: bounded queue length in seconds of work

autoscale.description: server/worker/llm: target-tracking autoscaling; `instances` is the starting size

warmupS.description: launch → serving, seconds (default 30; EC2 ASG 90–180, k8s pod 5–20)

cooldownS.description: wait after scaling before scaling in (default 60)

warmupS.description: cache/cdn: re-warm time constant after a restart or flush (default 20 s)

writePolicy.description: cache/cdn: writes go on to the origin (through, default), or are acknowledged at the cache and flushed ~5 s later — fast, but lost if the cache dies first (behind)

workingSetGb.description: archive: the data it holds, GB (default 1,000), priced per GB-month; cache: the data it fronts, GB — with it the hit rate follows from the cache size (S 6.4, M 13, L 26 GB) and `skew`

skew.description: cache: how concentrated reads are on popular keys (Zipf exponent, default 1)

shards.description: db/replica: horizontal partitions, each a full database of its own — capacity and cost × shards; keys are spread by hash (give a sharded database's replica the same count)

hotKeyShare.description: db/kv: share of its traffic on one key (a celebrity, a hot counter): it all lands on one shard, which saturates first

partitions.description: stream: partitions (default 4) — 1,000 messages/s in each, and a subscriber can use at most one consumer instance per partition

refreshS.description: search: how often the index refreshes, s (default 1) — a document is searchable only after the next refresh; a longer interval indexes faster but searches miss recent writes for longer

edgeShare.description: edge: the share of requests the edge function answers itself (default 0.5: redirects, auth checks, cached personalisation); the rest go on to the origin

cpuMs.description: edge: CPU time per request, ms (default 1; exponentially spread)

cpuLimitMs.description: edge: the platform's CPU limit per request, ms (default 10 as Workers Free; about 1 for CloudFront Functions, 30,000 for Workers paid) — requests past it are killed with an error

retrieval.description: archive: how a read gets its object back — instant (default: milliseconds, Glacier Instant Retrieval, 5,500 reads/s), or a Glacier Flexible Retrieval restore: expedited (1–5 min, $10 per 1,000) or standard (3–5 h) at 1,000 restores/s

recall.description: vector: the recall queries are tuned for (default 0.95) — each halving of the neighbours a search may miss doubles its work: 0.99 costs five times 0.95

vectorsM.description: vector: vectors in the index, millions (default 1; 768 dimensions, 3.5 GB of graph a million) — what does not fit in the nodes' memory (4/8/16 GB a node by size) is read from disk at ~10× the cost

ttlS.description: dns: how long clients cache an answer, s (default 60) — a dead target keeps getting traffic until it expires

healthCheckS.description: dns: how long health checks take to notice a dead target, s (default 30; 3 checks × 10 s)

threads.description: server/worker: threads per instance — every request in flight holds one, waiting on its calls included (thread-per-request, e.g. Tomcat 200). Unset: asynchronous, waiting holds nothing

bulkhead.description: calls that may wait on any one dependency at once, per instance; past it a call fails at once instead of taking another thread

bulkheadWaitMs.description: with a bulkhead: how long a call past it waits for a slot before it fails, ms (default 0: fails at once, as Resilience4j's maxWaitDuration; a connection pool's acquire timeout is one, HikariCP's connectionTimeout 30,000) — the wait holds the caller's thread

provisioned.description: function: provisioned concurrency — executions kept warm, so no cold start up to it; billed by the hour whether used or not ($0.0000041667 per GB-s)

prefixes.description: storage: key prefixes the objects are spread over (default 10) — S3 takes 5,500 reads or 3,500 writes a second per prefix; `hotKeyShare` puts that share on one prefix

hotRowShare.description: db: share of the writes that update one row (a stock counter, a balance): its lock takes them one at a time, each for a write's time — at most 1,000 ÷ latency a second, however big the database

failoverS.description: db: seconds from the primary dying to a replica taking writes (default 60, RDS Multi-AZ: 60–120 s; Aurora under 30 s; Cloud SQL HA about 60 s). Reads go on to the replicas meanwhile; with no automatic failover, the time someone takes to promote one by hand

burst.description: gateway: the token bucket's size in requests (default one second of `limit`): a burst above the rate passes until the bucket is empty — API Gateway's rate 10,000 and burst 5,000

maxReceives.description: queue: a redrive policy (SQS maxReceiveCount) — a message a consumer fails comes back after `visibilityS`, until it has been received this many times, then goes to the dead-letter queue; unset, a failed message is gone

visibilityS.description: queue: how long a received message stays hidden before it can be received again, s (default 30, as SQS)

maxConnections.description: lb/gateway: connections it can hold at once; each request holds one for `connectionS` (a websocket session, a streamed answer, a long poll) — past it, new ones are refused (Erlang B)

connectionS.description: lb/gateway: how long each request holds its connection, s (default 30)

everyS.description: client: a scheduled job instead of users (a cron, a nightly export) — every everyS seconds it sends `batch` requests over `batchS` (default 10 s), the first run 10 s in; it takes no share of the user traffic, and its requests do not count as the users'

batch.description: client with everyS: requests per run

batchS.description: client with everyS: how long a run takes to send them, s (default 10)

latencyMs.description: network round trip added to every call over this link (cross-AZ ≈ 1, cross-region ≈ 60–150)

calls.description: calls per request over this link, made in parallel; the caller needs every one (a tweet written to N timelines, N lookups per page)

carries.description: the link takes only reads or only writes (CQRS: reads to a cache or replica, writes to a queue); default both

replication.description: database → replica: sync — every write waits for this replica (no data lost on failover, writes stop while it is unreachable); async (default) — the replica lags, a failover loses what it had not received

reconnect.description: seconds the caller keeps failing its calls over this link after the callee comes back from being down: a client connection that stays broken (gRPC reconnect backoff, a channel that gave up). "until-restart": until the caller itself restarts. Unset or 0: it reconnects at once. An assumption you state, not something measured

connections.description: caller → callee pairs, e.g. "lb -> api", ["lb","api"] or { from, to, latencyMs }; order matters for failover routing

members.description: component ids located in this failure domain

sections.description: sections on the board: a labelled frame around components, for reading the design ("checkout path"); unlike a zone it is not a failure domain, and the engines ignore it

notes.description: notes on the board: free text at a position, for explaining the design; the engines ignore them
